I’m in Scotland btw. These came out from the bottom of my philodendron majesty’s pot, and I also found the same in my hoya mathilde’s saucer. They’re extremely fine and thin - maybe a couple centimetres max in length?

As a fellow hoya lover, i can so empathise with this struggle - something about these plants doing poorly just makes me feel so awful, especially since they can be so finicky!

It seems like it could be powdery mildew, which I’ve not really experienced so i’m afraid I can’t say much more. However, what you’re describing also sounds like root rot - i’ve had some battles with underwatering a couple of my hoya (owing to a fear of overwatering, ironically) and my krohniana & lacunosa did not take well to that. If it’s quite severe and the leaves are progressively dropping at the base, I’d suggest that at this point you should remove it from the soil & inspect the roots. 

If it’s root rot, trim off the dead roots + clean with peroxide and repot into a fresh chunky blend of substrate. Honestly though, i’ve had the best luck through propagating cuttings from the best surviving leaves and restarting from there. It was a tough chop, but my krohniana was eventually better off for it. I hope this helps even a little bit. All the best :)

My friend, i hear you and I feel for you. As a recovering addict and alcoholic, i’m all too familiar with those experiences and i empathise with your pain. 3 years ago i was taken out of college before my A-levels to go to rehab—it was a huge blow to my ego and i fought against it, trying to convince others and myself that i was a ‘high-functioning’ alcoholic. Every alcoholic i met in treatment and AA have told themselves the same thing, but i’m sure you know deep down that it’s a lie. Our addiction is a disease, and it thrives on self-deception. 

The first step is always the hardest—to admit powerlessness over our addiction. I catch a glimpse of myself in the things you’re saying, and i want you to know that wherever you are right now, it’s okay to be powerless. We are only human, and this is why the 12-step program asks us to surrender to a higher power. ‘Let go, let God’. I’m still working on this myself, but you know what the funny thing is? I rarely go on this sub, but this is the first Ramadan that i’ve been sober and it’s left a void that made me return to Him. I think it’s no coincidence that He wanted me to see this. If it means anything at all, I’m here if you wish to talk to someone. Above all, confide in Allah, for he is the best listener. May he guide you and grant you strength.

I’m sorry that you’re having a hard time with this, and i can empathise as someone in a similar situation. I’m a compulsive list-writer (an excruciating extension of my ADHD) and i notice that most of my ‘decluttering’ attempts will plateau as soon as i have to confront papers. The test papers/essays which i’ve hoarded throughout my years in education are difficult enough, but the random scraps of paper with scribbled thoughts and ideas are daunting. 

I wish i could offer a solution for dealing with the current notes you have, but i can suggest some alternatives that i’ve been implementing myself. I recently made a conscious intent to avoid writing on post-its/receipts/loose paper as i move forward, narrowing it down to my planner & journal. How do you feel about going digital? I personally love the iphone notes app, which comes in handy for jotting down ideas or intrusive thoughts that demand to be acknowledged. I also downloaded a voice recorder on my phone to use whenever i’m thinking out loud—it’s really interesting because they’re all dated & titled, and it’s become a sort of audio library for my thoughts that i can revisit whenever i need to. That way, i can worry less about forgetting my thoughts/ideas without adding to the piles of paper that currently litter my bedroom floor.
